picks.headline: Qualcomm's next Snapdragon flagship chip wants your AI agents to stay on-device
picks.excerpt: Qualcomm detailed the NPU in the upcoming Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6, pitching a big jump in on-device model capacity. Qualcomm says the chip will run bigger models with ease so agents can work locally instead of round-tripping to the cloud.
picks.rationale: Sets the 2027 Android baseline for how much agent work runs locally — the number product teams will design latency and privacy assumptions around.

picks.headline: Quest's Meta Virtual Display Got A New Name, Input Forwarding & Mac Parity
picks.excerpt: Meta's Quest virtual monitor feature was renamed and gained input forwarding, with the Mac version now matching Windows functionality. It makes a headset a more usable second display for desk work.
picks.rationale: Input forwarding plus Mac parity is the point where a headset becomes a real second monitor for design work, not a demo.

picks.headline: The HONOR Robot Phone feels like the first phone I'd actually buy for its weirdest feature
picks.excerpt: Hands-on with HONOR's Robot Phone, whose motorized gimbal camera module turns the handset into a semi-autonomous camera operator. The oddest part of the design turns out to be the most convincing reason to buy it.
picks.rationale: A motorized gimbal module that makes the phone operate its own camera is the boldest hardware-form argument of the week, and the hands-on says it works.

picks.headline: FCC Grants First Robotics Ban Exemption to a Robomower Company
picks.excerpt: The FCC granted its first exemption under the new robotics restrictions, clearing Swedish robot mower maker Husqvarna to sell new products in the US. It sets the first precedent for how autonomous home robots get to market.
picks.rationale: First precedent for how autonomous home robots clear the new US restrictions — it decides which hardware roadmaps are shippable at all.

picks.headline: Apple confirms Siri AI launches in English this month, will add five languages in October
picks.excerpt: Apple confirmed the rollout timeline for the rebuilt Siri AI, launching in English alongside iOS 27 before expanding to five more languages in October. It will not ship in China or the EU at launch.
picks.rationale: A confirmed date and language list — plus no EU or China at launch — tells teams exactly when and where they can rely on Siri AI in a flow.
